implementation_notes: C# has two local answers and they are better than a helper class. First, `this` extension method: a static class of extension methods called as if they were members of the target type gives the discoverability without the object, and it is the standard way to add behaviour to a type you cannot modify. Second, if the class is doing initialisation work in its constructor, move the work into a static factory on the class that owns the state. Note that a static class of extension methods over a wide target type is itself heading toward a utility class — keep each extension in the class whose types it operates on.
idiom_name: class with only a constructor; extension method as the replacement
pitfalls: A `*Helper` static class accumulating extension methods across unrelated types is the utility-class rescue, not the cure.
`async void` helpers that fire-and-forget work have real lifetime and failure semantics and are not poltergeists.
Extension methods on your own sealed types are a design smell in their own right — put the method on the type.
